decisions.reasoning: This convergence is fundamentally about how local data determines global properties through cohomological functors. The claim is best captured by showing that cohomology functors establish a categorical equivalence between local algebraic/analytic data and global geometric invariants, with the residue theorem as a special case of this general principle.

Category theory provides the framework for sheaf cohomology and derived functors that connect local-to-global phenomena. Topology is essential for defining sheaves and cohomology groups, while algebraic structures (rings, modules) form the local data being globalized.

decisions.choice: The proof attempts to use Čech cohomology to show that global sections and cohomology groups of coherent sheaves are determined by local data. It relies on vanishing theorems (Cartan B, Serre) to reduce computations to local intersections, but fails to establish that all geometric properties can be expressed cohomologically or that local algebraic relations suffice to determine global gluing.
